audit: Cohort A: 11 hypermutated cases (7 with >500 rows, up to 15,731, mostly 'Glioma, malignant' and 'Neoplasm, malignant') inflate passenger genes, so they were excluded from enrichment tests; 201 cases have non-specific labels ('missing', 'Unknown', 'Neoplasm...') and many diagnoses are tiny (n<10), so findings for small groups are fragile; gene fusions (KIAA1549-BRAF, PAX3/7-FOXO1), copy-number losses (SMARCB1 deletions) and other structural events are not captured, so pilocytic BRAF, alveolar RMS FOXO1 and ATRT SMARCB1 frequencies are underestimates; protein positions use a non-canonical transcript numbering (BRAF V600E appears as p.V640E, H3 K27M as p.K28M); recurrent identical missense calls in non-driver genes (e.g. ZNF510 p.Q248E, HLTF p.Q898E) look like germline/artifact calls. Cohort A otherwise looks like genuine pediatric tumor data with the expected driver-diagnosis links. Cohort B looks artificial/altered: its diagnosis mix is almost exactly half of cohort A's in every category, the site field is blank for all 572 cases, and the diagnosis labels appear decoupled from the mutations - none of the canonical associations replicate (H3-3A K27M, BRAF V600E, IDH1 R132H, DDX3X, PTCH1, SMARCB1, FGFR4 carriers are scattered across unrelated diagnoses; IDH1 R132H falls in medulloblastoma, ATRT/neuroblastoma median age 11-13 y). Instead it shows biologically implausible enrichments (ZNF510 p.Q248E in pilocytic astrocytoma, CACNA1H in medulloblastoma, HLTF p.Q898E in glioma, ATRX in medulloblastoma, TTN in ependymoma) that look planted or produced by label permutation; the same ZNF510/HLTF recurrent variants show no such enrichment in cohort A. I therefore report no claims for cohort B.
methods: For each cohort, cases with >500 non-synonymous rows were excluded from discovery; for every diagnosis with >=3 cases and every gene mutated in >=2 of its cases I computed a one-sided Fisher exact test of gene-mutated case fraction in that diagnosis versus all other cases (624 tests in A, 227 in B) with Benjamini-Hochberg adjustment. Claims were kept if they were strongly significant and/or biologically coherent with known pediatric tumor biology, and probabilities reflect both the statistical evidence and prior plausibility; expected frequencies are (k+0.5)/(n+1) over all cases of the diagnosis. Known-answer tasks were computed directly (BRAF V600E counted as p.V640E, H3-3A K27M as p.K28M given the transcript numbering). Cohort B data integrity checks (driver placement, label distribution, site field, age patterns) indicated altered labels, so no cohort B claims were made.
